construct: Nigrostriatal dopamine activates D1 receptors on direct-pathway medium spiny neurons. These neurons inhibit GPi/SNr, reducing inhibitory output from the basal ganglia to the VA/VL thalamus. Thalamocortical excitation therefore increases, facilitating movement.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Nigrostriatal dopamine activates D1 receptors on direct-pathway medium spiny neurons, increasing inhibition of GPi/SNr and disinhibiting motor thalamus to facilitate movement.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: D2 receptors are the most plausible competitor because they are also striatal dopamine receptors, but they are characteristic of the indirect pathway and dopamine inhibits those neurons.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The explicit direct projection to GPi and increased motor cortical output uniquely identify D1 receptor signaling.
